selector.rationale: Rapid onset of disorganized speech, severe anxiety, and self-harm behaviors, along with cognitive decline and hallucinations, are more consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, which is known for its rapid progression and diverse neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: cerebral venous thrombosis
rejected.why: Normal brain MRI and lack of typical symptoms such as headache or seizures

rejected.label: Primary progressive aphasia
rejected.why: While the patient has disorganized speech, the presence of other symptoms like hallucinations and significant cognitive decline suggests a more complex diagnosis

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: Lack of specific symptoms like alien limb syndrome or significant parkinsonism

rejected.label: Corticobasal syndrome
rejected.why: Similar to corticobasal degeneration, the absence of distinctive features makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: While some symptoms align, the rapid progression and combination of cognitive, psychiatric, and neurological symptoms point more towards Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease

contradict_spans: A 74-year-old right-handed woman was brought to the psychiatry clinic with a 5-month history of abrupt onset of disorganized speech, severe anxiety, and self-harm behaviors that began after a family trip
Her speech was rapid, fluent, and nonsensical—exemplified by the phrase “Our neighbor has gone to the cobbler to buy Ghormeh Sabzi”—consistent with Wernicke’s aphasia
An initial brain MRI performed 2 months after symptom onset was reported as normal
